Ergomed is a specialist clinical research organization focused on rare disease and select oncology indications. If you want work with purpose, the agility to make an impact and a team that cares about the people behind the work as much as the work itself, we would love to hear from you. Serves as the lead oncology strategist as assigned for potential awards and/or supports the other oncology-focused operational strategists as appropriate. Co-leads bid defense preparations with Business Development for assigned opportunities and participate in other client meetings as needed in collaboration with Business Development, the SVP, SSPC, and other Senior Operational staff. Develops strong relations with clients’ key decision makers by leveraging knowledge and expertise to drive repeat business for oncology and oncology-related opportunities and awards. Collaborates closely with other global functions, such as Project Management, Clinical Operations, Data Management, Statistics, Regulatory and Safety as per the scope of the opportunity. Supports functional teams to enhance client relations and ensure high customer satisfaction. Support business development and marketing activities by participating in conferences and meetings and generating marketing content such as webinars and white papers as part of Ergomed Group’s overall marketing strategy. Qualifications Degree in a life science or another related field, or equivalent education and experience. Advanced degree preferred. Extensive experience in clinical research within a CRO with strong oncology experience Demonstrated experience at a senior level contributing to project oversight and delivery Proven track-record in maintaining, developing and strengthening customer relations Previous experience in an oncology strategy position preferred Additional Information When you join Ergomed Group, you make a difference by helping to bring safe and effective pharmaceutical treatment to patients around the world. You’ll join a passionate and collaborative team of experts in clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and quality consulting. We are diverse in many ways, yet our values unite us. Our values are how we work, not words on a wall. If they sound like you, you will feel at home here. Quality: we hold ourselves to the standard patients deserve. Integrity and trust: we do the right thing, especially when it is hard. Drive and passion: we care about the outcome, because someone is waiting on it. Agility and responsiveness: we move quickly, because patients cannot wait. Belonging: everyone is welcome, and every voice counts. Collaborative partnerships: we go further by going together. We look forward to welcoming your application.

review_candidates.title: Senior Counterparty Exposure Measurement Specialist
review_candidates.description: Job Title: Senior Counterparty Exposure Measurement Specialist Location: UAE (Remote) Employment Type: Full-Time Work Arrangement: Fully Remote Level: Senior About Us We are seeking an experienced and analytical Senior Counterparty Exposure Measurement Specialist to measure, monitor, and manage counterparty credit exposures across financial transactions, derivatives, securities financing, and other relevant portfolios. This role supports effective credit risk management by ensuring exposure calculations are accurate, risk-sensitive, and aligned with internal risk policies and applicable regulatory requirements. The successful candidate will collaborate with counterparty credit risk, trading, treasury, collateral management, quantitative analytics, and regulatory reporting teams to identify potential exposure concentrations, assess risk mitigation effectiveness, and strengthen exposure monitoring and reporting processes. Key Responsibilities Exposure Measurement: Calculate and monitor current exposure, potential future exposure (PFE), expected exposure, and other relevant counterparty credit risk measures across financial products and portfolios. Counterparty Risk Analysis: Assess exposures to banks, financial institutions, corporates, brokers, clearing houses, and other counterparties. Derivatives Exposure: Analyze counterparty exposures arising from interest rate swaps, foreign exchange contracts, credit derivatives, equity derivatives, and other over-the-counter and exchange-traded products. Securities Financing: Measure exposures associated with repurchase agreements, reverse repos, securities lending, and margin lending transactions where applicable. Netting and Collateral: Evaluate the impact of legally enforceable netting agreements, collateral arrangements, margin requirements, and other credit risk mitigation mechanisms on exposure calculations. Potential Future Exposure Modeling: Support the development, calibration, and application of exposure models that estimate potential changes in counterparty exposure over relevant time horizons. Exposure Aggregation: Consolidate counterparty exposures across trading desks, legal entities, portfolios, products, and jurisdictions while accounting for applicable netting arrangements. Limit Monitoring: Monitor exposures against approved counterparty credit limits, investigate limit breaches, and escalate material exceptions according to internal procedures. Risk Concentration Analysis: Identify significant exposures, correlated counterparties, sector concentrations, and vulnerabilities arising from market movements or changes in counterparty credit quality. Stress Testing: Conduct scenario analysis and stress testing to assess how adverse market conditions, volatility changes, and counterparty deterioration may affect exposure levels. Data Reconciliation: Reconcile exposure calculations with trading systems, collateral records, risk engines, and financial reporting outputs to identify and resolve discrepancies. Regulatory Compliance: Support counterparty credit risk measurement and reporting under applicable UAE requirements and relevant Basel standards, including counterparty credit risk and exposure measurement frameworks where appropriate. Model and Methodology Review: Assist with reviewing exposure methodologies, model assumptions, calculation logic, and risk measurement limitations. Reporting and Analytics: Prepare regular exposure reports, dashboards, limit utilization summaries, and management analysis for credit risk committees and senior stakeholders. Systems and Automation: Work with technology and quantitative teams to improve exposure calculation processes, data integration, system controls, and reporting automation. Governance and Documentation: Maintain accurate methodology documentation, exposure records, limit exception logs, reconciliation evidence, and audit trails. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with front-office, middle-office, collateral, legal, finance, and risk teams to resolve exposure issues and improve risk controls. Technical Guidance: Provide guidance to junior analysts and contribute to consistent exposure measurement practices across the organization. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Financial Engineering, Quantitative Finance, or a related discipline. A master's degree in a quantitative or financial discipline is an advantage. At least 5–8 years of relevant experience in counterparty credit risk, exposure measurement, derivatives risk, collateral risk, or quantitative financial risk management. Strong understanding of current exposure, potential future exposure, expected exposure, exposure at default (EAD), and related counterparty risk concepts. Practical knowledge of derivatives, securities financing transactions, collateral arrangements, margining, and legally enforceable netting agreements. Familiarity with Basel counterparty credit risk frameworks, including SA-CCR where applicable, is highly desirable. Experience with exposure simulation, market risk factors, scenario analysis, and quantitative exposure modeling is an advantage. Proficiency in Excel and SQL, with experience using Python, R, MATLAB, or similar analytical tools preferred. Familiarity with risk engines, trading platforms, collateral management systems, and counterparty credit risk reporting tools. Strong analytical, numerical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex exposure discrepancies. Understanding of risk governance, data quality controls, regulatory reporting, and audit documentation. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. High attention to detail, sound professional judgment, and the ability to work independently in a fully remote environment. Professional qualifications such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or relevant quantitative risk certifications are an advantage. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Performance will be assessed against agreed risk measurement, control, and reporting objectives, including: Exposure Calculation Accuracy: Accuracy and consistency of current exposure, potential future exposure, and related counterparty risk measures. Reporting Timeliness: Delivery of exposure reports and limit utilization updates within agreed deadlines. Limit Monitoring Effectiveness: Timely identification and escalation of counterparty exposure breaches and near-breaches. Reconciliation Quality: Reduction in unresolved discrepancies between risk systems, trading records, collateral data, and reporting outputs. Data Quality: Completeness, reliability, and traceability of inputs used in exposure calculations. Risk Concentration Identification: Effectiveness in identifying material exposure concentrations and emerging counterparty risks. Stress Testing Quality: Reliability and usefulness of scenario analysis and stressed exposure assessments. Regulatory Compliance: Adherence to applicable exposure measurement methodologies, reporting standards, and internal controls. Process Efficiency: Improvements in calculation speed, reporting automation, and operational efficiency. Documentation and Audit Readiness: Completeness of methodologies, reconciliation records, limit exception logs, and supporting evidence. Stakeholder Support: Effectiveness of collaboration with trading, credit risk, collateral management, and other relevant teams. What We Offer Competitive salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. Fully remote working arrangement based in the UAE. Opportunity to work on sophisticated counterparty credit risk measurement and exposure analytics. Exposure to derivatives, collateral management, regulatory frameworks, and enterprise risk governance. Professional development opportunities in quantitative risk, financial markets, and counterparty credit risk management. A collaborative working environment that values analytical rigor, accountability, and continuous improvement. How to Apply Interested candidates are invited to submit an updated CV highlighting their experience in counterparty exposure measurement, derivatives risk, potential future exposure modeling, collateral analysis, and regulatory risk reporting. Applicants are encouraged to include examples of exposure measurement improvements, reconciliation automation, risk limit monitoring enhancements, or quantitative modeling projects. Email Subject Line: Application – Senior Counterparty Exposure Measurement Specialist (UAE Remote) We welcome applications from qualified professionals who combine strong quantitative expertise with sound credit risk judgment and a commitment to accurate, transparent, and reliable counterparty exposure measurement.
